Title: Screen Share Interop (Cyrena)
Summary: JS adapter for navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia. Stateless from the .NET perspective: .NET owns the state graph (which chat has which source), JS holds N concurrent MediaStreams in a Map keyed by opaque tokens. Each capture is addressed by token, enabling multiple independent screen shares per document (e.g. chat A sharing monitor 2 while chat B shares a tab).
Content:
# Screen Share Interop

## Purpose

Browser screen-capture adapter for the Cyrena app. Lets Blazor components pick a screen/window/tab, hold that source alive across multiple captures, and address the source by a stable token. Designed for multi-chat scenarios where the same document hosts multiple independent screen shares.

## Architectural Model

- **State lives in .NET.** Tokens, labels, displaySurface classifications, and per-chat associations are .NET state.
- **JS holds the only real references to live `MediaStream` objects**, in a `Map<token, ActiveSource>` in module scope.
- **One document, many streams.** Multiple tokens can be active simultaneously. Each stream's lifetime is bounded by the document, not by any Blazor component.
- **No global "current source" singleton.** Every operation takes or returns a token.

## Why Tokens, Not Stream References

`MediaStream` is a browser-internal type that cannot be meaningfully serialized across the JS interop boundary. .NET cannot hold a direct reference to a `MediaStream` and call methods on it. The token is JS's contribution: an opaque string that .NET uses to say "the stream I asked for, with this label, that I associate with chat X." JS holds the actual stream; .NET holds the address.

## Why a Map, Not a Single Slot

Multiple chats can each have their own active source. A single module-scope stream slot would create an implicit mutex (picking a new source for chat A would destroy chat B's source). The Map makes streams first-class, addressable, and independently revocable.

## Enumeration Limitations (Important)

The browser does **not** expose a `getScreens()` API. The only ways to learn about available displays are:

- `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()` — prompts the user, the OS picker is the enumeration UI.
- `navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices()` — returns cameras/mics only. Never displays.
- `window.screen` — single viewport number, not a list.

The "list of available sources" must come from the user's prior picks, surfaced via `listStreams()`. There is no way to programmatically enumerate displays. This is a deliberate browser security model, not a missing feature.

## Surface (callable from C# via `IJSRuntime`)

All methods are async unless noted. All return a plain JSON-serializable object; .NET should deserialize into a POCO.

### `isSupported()`

Synchronous. Returns `boolean`. Used at component init to decide whether to render the share button.

### `requestShare(dotNetRef, preferences?)`

Prompts the OS picker, registers the resulting stream in the Map under a fresh token. Does **not** capture.

**Parameters:**
- `dotNetRef` — optional `DotNetObjectReference`. If provided, `OnStreamPicked` is invoked on it. .NET should pass a per-chat reference if multiple chats share this document.
- `preferences` — optional `{ displaySurface?: 'monitor'|'window'|'browser', audio?: boolean }`. `displaySurface` is a **hint**, not a filter — the picker still shows everything, but browsers may pre-select the indicated category.

**Returns:**
```typescript
{
  success: boolean,
  token?: string,           // present when success is true
  label?: string,           // e.g. "Display 2", "Firefox"
  displaySurface?: 'monitor'|'window'|'browser'|'unknown',
  width?: number,
  height?: number,
  cancelled?: boolean,      // present when user dismissed the picker
  error?: string            // present when success is false and not cancelled
}
```

**Side effects:** Fires `OnStreamPicked(token, label, displaySurface, width, height)` on `dotNetRef` if provided.

**Coalescing:** A second `requestShare` call for the same token (race / double-click) before the first picker resolves returns the same promise — one picker, one stream. Calls with different tokens get independent pickers, enabling concurrent picks from different chats.

### `captureStream(dotNetRef, token)`

Captures one frame from the stream identified by `token`. Does **not** stop the stream — it remains available for further captures.

**Returns:**
```typescript
{
  success: boolean,
  token: string,            // echoed back so .NET can correlate
  dataUrl?: string,         // base64 data URL, present when success is true
  fileName?: string,        // "screenshot-20260114-153022.png"
  mimeType?: string,        // "image/png"
  size?: number,            // bytes
  label?: string,
  displaySurface?: 'monitor'|'window'|'browser'|'unknown',
  sourceLost?: boolean,     // true when the stream has ended; token already removed from Map
  error?: string
}
```

**Side effects:** Fires `OnStreamCaptured(token, dataUrl, fileName, mimeType, size, label, displaySurface)` on `dotNetRef` if provided. The `OnFilePasted` callback used in the previous design is **renamed** to `OnStreamCaptured` and takes the token first.

**When the stream has ended:** Returns `sourceLost: true` and the token is no longer valid for further calls. .NET should clear the chat's source state and prompt the user to pick again.

### `changeStream(dotNetRef, token, preferences?)`

Stops the stream for `token`, opens the picker for a new one, registers the new stream under a **new token**. .NET must replace the old token with the new one in its state. The old token is invalidated.

**Returns:** Same shape as `requestShare`. The new token is in the `token` field.

### `releaseStream(dotNetRef, token)`

Stops the track and removes the Map entry. Safe to call with an unknown or already-released token (returns `released: false`). Does **not** fire any callback — the caller (usually .NET) initiated the release and is expected to update its own state.

Use from C#:
- `IDisposable.DisposeAsync` / `OnAfterRender` cleanup on a Blazor component
- User clicking an in-app "Stop sharing" button

**Returns:** `{ released: boolean }`

### `releaseAllStreams()`

Bulk teardown. No callbacks fired. Returns `{ released: number }` (count removed). Use on page unload if you want explicit cleanup; the browser reclaims the OS share indicator automatically on unload regardless.

### `listStreams()`

Synchronous snapshot of currently-held streams, for state reconciliation (e.g. after a Blazor Server reconnect) or to seed a re-pick UI.

**Returns:**
```typescript
[
  {
    token: string,
    label: string | null,
    displaySurface: 'monitor'|'window'|'browser'|'unknown',
    width: number,
    height: number,
    readyState: 'live' | 'ended'
  }
]
```

## .NET Callbacks (Invoked on the dotNetRef)

### `OnStreamPicked(token, label, displaySurface, width, height)`

Fired once per successful `requestShare` or `changeStream`. .NET is expected to store this in its state, associating `token` with the chat or view that initiated the pick.

### `OnStreamCaptured(token, dataUrl, fileName, mimeType, size, label, displaySurface)`

Fired after each successful `captureStream`. The data is the same shape the paste/drop pipeline already consumes; routing it into an existing `IFileHandler` is the expected integration point. `token` is included so the receiving component can correlate the capture with the chat that requested it.

### `OnStreamEnded(token)`

Fired when a stream's track fires `ended` — the user clicked the browser's "Stop sharing" indicator, the source window closed, the monitor was unplugged, etc. The token is **already removed from the Map** at this point. .NET should clear its state for that token and update the UI to show the chat as not-sharing.

## Recommended .NET State Model

```csharp
public sealed record ScreenShareState(
    string? Token,             // null when not sharing
    string? Label,
    string? DisplaySurface,
    int Width,
    int Height);

// Per chat, or per view, or per whatever the app's domain is:
public sealed class ChatState
{
    public ScreenShareState Share { get; set; } = new(null, null, null, 0, 0);
    // ... other chat state
}
```

## Lifetime Notes

- Streams survive Blazor page navigations that don't unload the document (SPA route change). This is what lets chat A's screen share persist when the user navigates chat B into view.
- Streams are reclaimed on full page unload.
- .NET is responsible for calling `releaseStream` in component `Dispose`/`DisposeAsync` paths. Failing to do so leaks the stream in the browser (and the user sees the "Stop sharing" indicator indefinitely).
- After a Blazor Server reconnect, call `listStreams()` and reconcile the resulting set against C# state; remove C# entries for tokens that no longer exist in the Map.

## Multi-Monitor Behavior

The browser's OS picker lists every available display, window, and tab as a separate entry. The user picks one. JS holds one stream for that one source. If the user wants to share multiple monitors simultaneously, they pick monitor 1, JS holds stream A under token T1; then they pick monitor 2, JS holds stream B under token T2. Two streams, two tokens, two independent captures. There is no API to "stitch" multiple monitors into one capture in a web app — that requires Electron/Tauri or similar with native display enumeration.

## Browser Quirks Worth Knowing

- **`displaySurface` setting in `track.getSettings()`** is the authoritative source for what the user picked, when the browser reports it. Chrome and Edge populate it; Firefox and Safari often don't. The fallback is label sniffing (looking for "screen", "display", "monitor" in the track label).
- **`ImageCapture.takePhoto()`** throws on some Chromium versions for tab-captured streams with hardware-protected video. The adapter falls back to a `<video>`+`<canvas>` pipeline in that case.
- **Persistent display capture permission** is a Chromium feature allowing re-capture without re-prompting. Not currently requested by this adapter; .NET can extend `requestShare`'s `preferences` to opt in if needed.
- **Audio from screen share** is exposed by the `audio: true` option in `preferences`. Default is false (video only) because most screenshot flows don't need mic/system audio in the same capture.
